papers.name: Paper 1 Depth Studies
instructions: Use black ink or ball-point pen.
Answer questions from TWO depth studies: one question for each depth study.
In part (c) of each question, answer EITHER (i) OR (ii).
Write your answers in the separate answer booklet.
Fill in the boxes on the front of the answer booklet.
information: The total mark for this paper is 60.
The marks for each question are shown in brackets: use this as a guide to how much time to spend on each question.
Spend about 45 minutes on each depth study.
advice: Read each question carefully before you start to answer it.
In part (a), refer closely to the extract and how the author presents the topic.
Check your answers if you have time at the end.

sections.title: Germany: development of dictatorship, 1918–45
sections.instructions: Answer parts (a) and (b), and EITHER (c)(i) OR (c)(ii).

sections.title: A world divided: superpower relations, 1943–72
sections.instructions: Answer parts (a) and (b), and EITHER (c)(i) OR (c)(ii).

Answer ONE question from Section A and ONE question from Section B.

information: The total mark for this paper is 60.
The marks for each question are shown in brackets: use this as a guide to how much time to spend on each question.
Spend about 45 minutes on each section.
advice: Read each question carefully before you start to answer it.
In Section A, use the sources and the extract as the question directs.
Check your answers if you have time at the end.

sections.instructions: Answer all parts of the question.

options.name: America: from new nation to divided union, 1783–1877

subtopics.title: The establishment of the Weimar Republic and its early problems
subtopics.summary: How the Kaiser fell, how the new republic was set up and the crises it faced up to 1923.

points.summary: The end of the monarchy and the revolution of 1918–19.
How the Weimar Constitution worked and its weaknesses.
German reactions to the Treaty of Versailles.
Threats from the left and right, such as the Spartacists and the Kapp Putsch.
The occupation of the Ruhr in 1923.
Hyperinflation and its effects on different groups.

subtopics.title: The recovery of Germany, 1924–29
subtopics.summary: How Stresemann helped Germany recover at home and abroad in the 'golden years'.

points.summary: Stresemann's role and achievements.
Economic recovery: the Rentenmark, the Dawes and Young Plans and American loans.
Foreign policy: Locarno, the League of Nations and the Kellogg–Briand Pact.

subtopics.title: The rise of Hitler and the Nazis to January 1933
subtopics.summary: How the Nazi Party grew from a tiny group into the largest party and Hitler became Chancellor.

points.summary: The origins of the Nazi Party.
Changes to the party in 1920–22.
The Munich Putsch and its consequences.
Reorganising the party after 1924.
The impact of the Great Depression.
Nazi methods, propaganda and the SA.
Political deals of 1932 to January 1933.

subtopics.title: Nazi Germany 1933–39
subtopics.summary: How Hitler created a dictatorship and controlled German society and the economy.

points.summary: Steps to dictatorship, 1933–34.
Methods of control: the police state, censorship and propaganda.
Policies towards education, young people, women and the Churches.
Racial policy and the persecution of Jews.
Economic policy: reducing unemployment, the RAD, the DAF and Strength Through Joy.

subtopics.title: Germany and the occupied territories during the Second World War
subtopics.summary: Life in Germany during the war, the Holocaust, opposition and the collapse of the Reich.

points.summary: The treatment of Jews: ghettos, the Einsatzgruppen and the Final Solution.
The impact of war on the home front.
Opposition and resistance to the Nazis.
The defeat of Germany and the end of the Third Reich.

subtopics.title: Reasons for the Cold War
subtopics.summary: Why the wartime alliance broke down, including ideology, the conferences and Soviet control of Eastern Europe.

points.summary: Long-term rivalry and ideological differences.
Tensions within the wartime alliance.
The Tehran, Yalta and Potsdam conferences.
Soviet expansion in Eastern Europe.
The attitudes of Truman and Stalin.

subtopics.title: Early developments in the Cold War, 1945–49
subtopics.summary: How Europe divided into two blocs, from the 'iron curtain' to the Berlin Crisis and NATO.

points.summary: Soviet expansion and satellite states.
The 'iron curtain' speech.
The Truman Doctrine and the Marshall Plan.
Cominform and Comecon.
Disagreements over Germany and the creation of Bizonia.
The Berlin Crisis, NATO and the creation of two German states.

subtopics.title: The Cold War in the 1950s
subtopics.summary: The arms race, Khrushchev's peaceful co-existence and the crushing of the Hungarian Rising.

points.summary: The Korean War and the Warsaw Pact.
Khrushchev and peaceful co-existence.
Rákosi's rule and the causes of the Hungarian Rising.
The Soviet invasion of Hungary and its effects.
The nuclear arms race.

subtopics.title: Three Cold War crises: Berlin, Cuba and Czechoslovakia, c1957–69
subtopics.summary: The Berlin Wall, the Cuban Missile Crisis and the Prague Spring, and what they show about superpower relations.

points.summary: The U2 incident and the Paris Summit.
Reasons for building the Berlin Wall.
Effects of the Berlin Wall.
The Bay of Pigs and the Cuban Missile Crisis.
The Prague Spring, the invasion of Czechoslovakia and the Brezhnev Doctrine.

subtopics.title: The thaw and moves towards détente, 1963–72
subtopics.summary: How the superpowers tried to reduce tension after 1962, through to SALT I.

points.summary: The Hotline and the arms treaties of the 1960s.
Reasons for détente.
The SALT talks and SALT I.
How far relations had improved by 1972.

subtopics.title: Tsarist rule in Russia, 1905–14
subtopics.summary: The 1905 Revolution, the Dumas, Stolypin and growing discontent before the First World War.

points.summary: The nature of Tsarist rule and discontent.
Bloody Sunday, the Potemkin mutiny and the soviets.
The October Manifesto and why the Tsar survived 1905.
The Dumas and their limits.
Opposition groups.
Stolypin's repression and reforms.
The Lena Goldfields Massacre and rising unrest.

subtopics.title: Opposition to Tsarist rule, 1914–17
subtopics.summary: How the First World War weakened the Tsar and led to the February Revolution and his abdication.

points.summary: Effects of the war on the army and the home front.
Rasputin and the Tsarina.
Causes and events of the February Revolution.
Army mutiny and the Tsar's abdication.
The setting up of the Provisional Government.

subtopics.title: Provisional Government and the Bolshevik revolution, 1917
subtopics.summary: Why the Provisional Government failed and how the Bolsheviks seized power in October 1917.

points.summary: Weaknesses of the Provisional Government.
The Petrograd Soviet and Dual Power.
The April Theses and the July Days.
The Kornilov Affair.
The Bolshevik seizure of power.
Reasons for success, including Lenin and Trotsky.

subtopics.title: The Bolshevik consolidation of power and the Civil War, 1917–21
subtopics.summary: How the Bolsheviks kept power: early decrees, the Constituent Assembly, Brest-Litovsk and the Civil War.

points.summary: Early Bolshevik decrees.
The closing of the Constituent Assembly.
The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk.
The two sides in the Civil War.
Events of the Civil War and reasons for Bolshevik victory.

subtopics.title: War Communism and the New Economic Policy, 1918–24
subtopics.summary: Why War Communism was replaced by the NEP, opposition to it and Lenin's achievements by 1924.

points.summary: War Communism and its effects.
The Kronstadt Rising.
The New Economic Policy.
Opposition to the NEP.
Lenin's achievements by 1924.

topics.title: America: from new nation to divided union, 1783–1877

subtopics.title: A new nation, 1783–1803
subtopics.summary: How the United States created its Constitution and system of government, and the divisions this caused.

points.summary: Large and small states and the question of slavery.
Shays' Rebellion.
The Constitutional Convention and the Connecticut Compromise.
Federalists, Anti-federalists and the Bill of Rights.
Strict and loose constructionists.
Jefferson's presidency.

subtopics.title: Westward expansion, 1803–53
subtopics.summary: How and why the USA expanded across the continent, and the impact on Native Americans and slavery.

points.summary: Opposition to expansion.
The Louisiana Purchase, the Transcontinental Treaty and Texas.
The Missouri Compromise.
Indian Removal and the Trail of Tears.
Manifest Destiny, Oregon, the Mexican War and the Gold Rush.

subtopics.title: The road to civil war, 1850–61
subtopics.summary: How disputes over slavery and the territories divided North and South and led to secession.

points.summary: The Compromise of 1850.
The Kansas–Nebraska Act and Bleeding Kansas.
The Dred Scott decision.
Economic differences between North and South.
John Brown, Lincoln's election, secession and Fort Sumter.

subtopics.title: The Civil War, 1861–65
subtopics.summary: Why the Union won, the leaders on each side and the effects of the war on the South.

points.summary: Reasons for Union victory and the role of generals.
The Union blockade.
Lincoln, Davis, the Emancipation Proclamation and the Gettysburg Address.
Key battles and campaigns: Gettysburg, Vicksburg and the March through Georgia.
The impact of the war on the Southern economy.

subtopics.title: Reconstruction, 1865–77
subtopics.summary: How the South was rebuilt, what freedom meant for African Americans, and policy towards Native Americans.

points.summary: Johnson and the Reconstruction Acts.
The Freedmen's Bureau and the Black Codes.
The Civil Rights Acts and the 13th–15th Amendments.
The Peace Policy and the Battle of the Little Bighorn.
